claims.section: Ensuring Integrity and Protection of Data
claims.claim_text: Our Information Security Management System (ISMS), aligned with the ISO 27001 standard, undergoes internal reviews and external audits to ensure its effectiveness.
pack: ## Ensuring Integrity and Protection of Data Protecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data is fundamental to our cybersecurity strategy. We implement strict access controls, encryption protocols, and regular data backup and recovery procedures to safeguard sensitive information across all business units. Our Information Security Management System (ISMS), aligned with the ISO 27001 standard, undergoes internal reviews and external audits to ensure its effectiveness.

To strengthen our sustainability risk management, we conduct a biannual review of critical risk areas based on defined performance indicators. This includes cause analysis, consequence mapping, and evaluation of risk control plans, followed by the development of supplementary actions to maintain risks at acceptable levels. External audits further strengthen oversight, covering the identified risks, and include certifications such as ISO 45001 (Health and Safety), ISO 27001 (Information Technology), and Energy Management or the Resource and Efficiency Check (REC). Audits are conducted annually by internal teams or third-party experts to ensure continuous improvement.

# Environmental Management System (EMS) We implement an Environmental Management System (EMS) aligned with ISO 14001 standards to manage environmental responsibilities across our operations. Furthermore, our Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) team has a comprehensive compliance assurance auditing program, supported by third-party consultants with expertise in the regulatory requirements of the jurisdictions where we operate. The scope of these audits includes both EHS regulatory compliance and alignment with Corporate EHS standards. An audit schedule is maintained and reviewed annually. Each year, between 25 to 30 sites are audited by third-party consultants. Since the program's launch in 2022, 59 sites have been audited. In 2024, 80% of operations were certified, audited, and verified under ISO 14001. An additional 12% of operations, not yet certified, were audited by a third party, bringing total EMS verification and audit coverage to 92%.
Ensuring Integrity and Protection of Data
As of 2024, 50% of Indorama Ventures' operations are certified under the ISO 27001 standard.
Ensuring Integrity and Protection of Data
Since 2022, we have partnered with an external vendor to conduct VAPT, including comprehensive system assessments and simulated cyberattacks.

claims.claim_text: In 2024, SCG successfully reduced greenhouse gas emissions by 25.6%, showing significant progress relative to the SBTi targets.
pack: In 2024, SCG successfully reduced green- house gas emissions by 25.6%, showing significant progress relative to the SBTi targets. In addition, the Board of Directors appointed an Environmental Sustainability Development Committee to oversee and support initiatives in pursuit of the net-zero goals.

SCG has established both short-term and long-term greenhouse gas emission reduction targets in accordance with the Paris Agreement to limit global temperature rise to no more than 2 degrees Celsius, with efforts to keep it below 1.5 degrees Celsius by 2050, compared to pre-industrial levels. In 2021, SCG joined the Science Based Target initiative (SBTi), which certifies organizations' targets according to scientific calculation standards. In 2023, SCG received SBTi certification for its near-term targets to reduce GHG Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 25% by 2030 compared to the base year of 2020 and decrease GHG Scope 3 emissions from fossil fuel sales to external customers by at least 25% by 2031, compared to the base year of 2021.
SCG Decor upholds its commitment to achieving its Net Zero goal by 2050, with a short-term goal of reducing absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 25% by 2030 from the 2020 base year.

Furthermore, SCG has joined SBTi and received validation for its decarbonization targets: 25% reduction in GHG Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 compared to 2020 baseline, and at least 25% reduction in Scope 3 emissions from fossil fuel sales to external customers by 2031 compared to 2021 baseline. These targets demonstrate our commitment and how our operational approach can instill confidence among all stakeholders in our capability to achieve the established long-term goals.

SCG’s near-term SBTI-validated targets to reduce Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 25% by 2030 compared to the 2020 baseline and to lower Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel sales to external customers by at least 25% by 2031 compared to the 2021 baseline.

claims.claim_text: Furthermore, GC’s disclosure of information is in accordance with the guidelines of the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), namely IFSR S1 (Sustainability-related Disclosures) and IFRS S2 (Climate-related Disclosures), as well as other industry-based metrics.
pack: PTT Global Chemical Public Company Limited, or GC, has formulated the Integrated Sustainability Report to communicate corporate strategies, management systems, operational processes, and sustainability performance on issues of significance to GC's business operations and stakeholders from all sectors throughout the year. It also describes GC's progress and performance in supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This report has been prepared in accordance with GRI Standards. It has been reviewed by the Sustainable Development Committee and independent third-party agencies to verify and confirm its completeness, integrity and accuracy. For the Content Index – Essentials Service, GRI Services reviewed that the GRI content index has been presented in a way consistent with the requirements for reporting in accordance with the GRI Standards, and that the information in the index is clearly presented and accessible to the stakeholders. Furthermore, GC's disclosure of information is in accordance with the guidelines of the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), namely IFSR S1 (Sustainability-related Disclosures) and IFRS S2 (Climate-related Disclosures), as well as other industry-based metrics.

GC has defined the Energy Management and Climate Strategy in accordance with the guidelines of the International Financial Reporting Standards S2 (IFRS S2) - Climate-related Disclosures, focusing on three areas of operations, namely Efficiency-driven using modern technology, Portfolio-driven to shift towards High Value-Low Carbon Business, and Compensation-driven, in order to achieve the Net Zero Target and expand operations to cover other indirect emissions (Scope 3) across the value chain.

Under GC's climate governance structure, the Corporate Governance and Sustainability Committee and the Risk Management Committee are responsible for determining and monitoring the directions of climate change and decarbonization. GC has also appointed the Management Committee and the Sustainable Development Committee, which operate at the management level. In this regard, operating results are reported to the relevant committees on a quarterly basis.
